receipt.callable_reasoning: Authorizes actor then loads service. Optional Name normalized, rejects blank and detects other-ID name clash before Save. Updates fee only when nonnull, so nullable fee cannot be cleared to null through this request; Active optionally toggles. No monetary sign/max validation, no row concurrency token/name-admission lock, no historical order rewrite. Concurrent updates can be last-writer-wins and name predicate races; no live DB acceptance claimed.

conclusion: The exact receipt reasoning is supported by current baseline source: authorization and optional approval precede target lookup; optional name is normalized/nonblank and collision-checked by read-before-save; supplied FeePiastres is assigned raw without a sign/magnitude bound; null is treated as no-op; Active is optional; handler saves configuration only. Active query returns stored fee, Cashier can place selected fee in checkout request, checkout converts to Money, and CheckoutRules adds signed fee then clamps payable below zero. Ordinary management UI rejects negative fee, so this is an API validation gap conditional on owner-confirmed fee policy, and it overlaps FIN-016; no separate finding. The test titled frozen-order snapshot changes a different service and checks DeliveryServiceId only; it does not prove the same-service numeric fee snapshot. No runtime effect, duplicate payment, or concurrency outcome established.
